title: Analyze Your Research Profile with ORCID
subtitle: Learn how to analyze all your research publications using your ORCID ID
about_body: This tutorial guides you step by step through analyzing your entire research profile using your ORCID ID. ORCID (Open Researcher and Contributor ID) is a unique identifier that lets the system automatically pull all your publications from multiple sources.

steps.title: Get Your ORCID ID
steps.description: If you don't have an ORCID ID yet, visit orcid.org and register for free. The signup process takes only a few minutes.

steps.title: Copy Your ORCID ID
steps.description: An ORCID ID looks like 0000-0000-0000-0000 (16 digits with hyphens). Make sure you copy the entire ID including the hyphens.

steps.title: Enter the ORCID ID on the Platform
steps.description: Return to our platform and enter your ORCID ID in the search field. Click "Analyze" to start.

steps.title: Review the Analysis Results
steps.description: The platform will pull all publications linked to your ORCID ID and run the SDG classification. You'll see a list of publications with confidence scores and SDG categories.

steps.title: Export and Share the Results
steps.description: You can export the analysis in multiple formats (CSV, Excel, PDF) or share it directly from the platform for further collaboration.

tips: Make sure your ORCID ID is linked to all your publications in the ORCID database.
If any publications are missing, add them manually via your ORCID account before running the analysis.
Use the full ORCID ID format with hyphens (e.g. 0000-0002-1825-0097).
The analysis may take a few seconds depending on how many publications you have.
format_body: An ORCID ID always consists of 16 digits split into 4 groups separated by hyphens.
cta_body: Start analyzing your research publications right now using your ORCID ID.
